text: A generation decision carries one of three final calls: GENERATED for a notice that was produced, HELD for a notice held on a missing merge value or a withdrawn template, and REFUSED for a generation refused because the template has no Approved version. The set is read from the reference list at the version in force and is never a literal.
why: DF-DEC-012 final_call is required on every entry, and no source states the final-call values of a D7.1 generation decision; the three values used are the notice states Generated and Held of RWB-E1-052 section 9 and the refusal of RWB-E1-052 AC2.
read: RWB-E1-052 sections 7, 9 and 14; FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-010-01, AC-EXC-P7-010-01 and AC-EXC-P7-010-03; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-012)
confirm: Product owner of rwb-decision with Legal, before the wave 1 build of the ledger slice
impact: A wrong set changes the entry of every notice and the reference list LOV-DECISION companion; it changes no rule and no notice state.

text: The capability area, the right and the scope of the two decision-log reads are declared on the operations and enforced at gateway-bff through the composite route of DP-19, which asks rwb-access; this story adds no guard, holds no role or scope row and makes no authorise call.
why: The right of the two reads is fixed by TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 and T6.1 but the mechanism of enforcement in the target is not stated for rwb-decision, and every other P7 story of the realignment places it at the edge.
read: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1, T6.1 and T6.2; Architecture v5 slide 8 and slide 13 notes; DP-08 and DP-19 of the DP table
confirm: Platform edge owner with rwb-access, at the RWB-PLT-N001-CON review
impact: If a guard belongs in the service, one component and one contract call are added and the scenarios of AC9 do not change.

text: The rule version label of R-LIT-03 and R-LIT-04 is read from the rule registry at the version in force; the label LIT-2026.12 named by FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-015-01 for a generated demand notice is used in the criteria as the version in force of the test data.
why: The legacy story writes the rule id and the template version on the entry but never a rule version label, and the entry requires one under BR5.
read: FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-015-01 and AC-P7-022-01; Drools design slide 6 and slide 16; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-005)
confirm: Rule owner of the litigation rule package, at the first rule promotion under RWB-P7-E1073-APP
impact: The label is data read from the registry, so a change of label changes no code and no criterion.

text: The generation entry carries the merge snapshot as an opaque reference inside inputs_ref, together with the template code and version and the ACE data date; the snapshot itself, with the merge code, the view column, the business key and the field ID of each value, stays with rwb-comms.
why: BR12 of the legacy story fixes the content of the snapshot and forbids the value, but no source names the store of the snapshot or the column that holds its reference.
read: RWB-E1-052 BR12 and section 4 step 7; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-008 inputs_ref); RWB-P6-E1052-APP section 11
confirm: TechX with the data steward, at the RWB-P6-E1052-CON review
impact: If the snapshot needs a column of its own, one migration step and one field are added to the entry; no rule changes.

text: This story is the rwb-decision slice of the split of RWB-E1-052: it appends the D7.1 generation record written by rwb-comms through the decision-record library to decision_log_entry, serves the two decision-log reads, and leaves the notice, the template, the merge values, the PDF, the task and the dispatch with their owners.
why: The legacy key is split across P6, P5, P3 and P7 and no source states which slice appends the generation record to the central ledger; the split is read from Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41, which give the ledger and its reads to rwb-decision.
read: Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 13, 14, 28 and 41; FSD P7 v3 A2.10 and feature row FEAT-DRI-14; RWB-P6-E1052-APP section 1
confirm: Service owner of rwb-decision with the P6 owner, at the Service Contract Catalog review
impact: If the append belongs to the producer instead, this story shrinks to the two reads and the ledger contract; the criteria of section 7 move to RWB-P6-E1052-APP.

text: MSG-P7-009 is the refusal message of a record that fails the schema check of the append, and its text is left to the message catalogue and the Thai message set of DL10; the placeholder of section 14 stands until the catalogue carries it.
why: FSD P7 v3 names MSG-P7-009 in its exception criteria and no document writes its text.
read: FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01, AC-EXC-P7-002-05 and AC-ALT-P7-002-01; Decision Log v10 (DL10)
confirm: Message catalogue owner, before the wave 1 system test
impact: Text only; no criterion and no field changes.

text: The platform contracts the DP table adds for this story (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and the decision-log and rule-registry baselines of the service are wave-0 and wave-1 work in place before the build, so the metadata build row stays None and the story is Day 1.
why: R5.7 gives Day 1 to a story with no H dependency on another non-contract story of its lane, and the DP table adds only platform CON rows.
read: R5.5 DP-03, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19; R5.7 rules 1, 2 and 8; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T5.3
confirm: Platform delivery lead, at the wave 1 gate
impact: If a platform contract slips, the story becomes After that contract and the lane is unchanged.
